patch_description: Gen 10 showed that pure beam search (289 makespan) beats variants with local search layered on top (292), because local search consumes wall-clock budget that is better spent on more beam search restarts with larger beams. This rewrite drops the local search entirely and instead converts all spare compute into beam search restarts: it keeps running beam searches (with randomized seed transactions and full lookahead expansion over remaining transactions, evaluated by actual `get_opt_seq_cost`) in a loop until a 25-second wall-clock budget is exhausted. Each restart's beam members are recorded as candidates, and the best full schedule found is returned. Since beam search greedily builds schedules by actual makespan cost, more restarts with wider beams directly sample the space of good prefix orderings, which is the dimension that demonstrably improves the makespan.
